tour.title: Workbench Entry Point
tour.description: Start with README.md to learn what this repository is: the Devere/TCS Digital Twin PM Package workbench. It explains the current control position, the start-here pointers, the boundary between review-ready vs. waiting-for-reviewer status, and the evidence discipline that governs every artifact in the repo. This is the orientation document a new agent or human reads before touching anything else.

tour.title: Digital Twin Doctrine - Floor and Ceiling
tour.description: The two doctrine specs define the standard every project digital twin in the workbench must meet. The FLOOR standard fixes the required hierarchy, twin contents, state fields, lifecycle, and readiness scale. The CEILING spec extends to portfolio/project twin architecture, source authority resolver, human-AI composite PM, SME networks, event sourcing, simulation, and the OpenFoundry maturity ladder. Together they bracket what 'good' looks like for any project under this standard.

tour.title: Agent Boot Sequence
tour.description: Building on the doctrine from Step 2, this is the boot document a new PM agent reads first when joining the UK CAER package. It defines the product frame, read order, source authority, gate posture, training duties, and a concrete first-60-minute checklist. Treat it as the on-ramp from doctrine into operational work.

tour.title: Control Plane - Command Center and Master Control
tour.description: These two READMEs describe the day-to-day control surface for the package. The Command Center owns the hot sheet, P0/P1 actions, and risk board; the Master Control README defines the master rule, workbook tabs, CPO approval record, and the operating boundary. After boot, this is where the agent actually drives work from.

tour.title: 9-Gate Readiness and A1/A2 Closure
tour.description: Gate readiness is the spine of the package. The 9-Gate Readiness Board reads each gate's status; the A1/A2 Evidence Closure Packet, Receipt Validation Ledger, and Sage Verification Package together carry the gate-closure evidence stack for the first two gates. Read these together to understand how a single gate gets from 'candidate' to 'closed' with receipts.

tour.title: Procurement Activation - B1/B2 Gate
tour.description: The B1/B2 Procurement Activation Board is the next gate the package has to clear. Its README defines purpose, current read, controls included, source chain, and the next safe action for activating procurement. This is the operational pattern any later gate board will reuse.

tour.title: Validation Pipeline
tour.description: Every artifact in the package has to pass validation before it can change a gate. The Validation Architecture and QC Plan defines the state model and QC rules; the Validation Queue and Zone Assignments routes individual validations across owners and zones; the Validation Zone Board renders the queue for daily ops. This is the quality discipline that protects the gate evidence from Step 5.

tour.title: Operational Risk - High-Risk Trade Packets
tour.description: Once gates and validation are in place, the day-to-day risk lives in specific trades. The High-Risk Trade Issue Packets README indexes each trade packet with counts, approval boundary, workbook tabs, and a recommended review sequence. This is where validated gate data turns into actionable trade-level decisions.

tour.title: Owner-Facing Reporting
tour.description: The Owner Progress Review package is what the owner actually sees. It defines the owner-view segmentation rule and the four visual flows (owner review, human PM bring-on, TCS control loop, validation discipline) that tie the internal control plane back to an external narrative. Everything in Steps 4-8 ultimately feeds this report.

tour.title: Build Tooling - Python and Node Builders
tour.description: All the workbooks and boards referenced above are generated by sibling Python builders plus a Node master-control builder. build_uk_caer_pm_command_center.py emits the Command Center workbook (hot sheet, action register, source register); build_uk_caer_pm_package.py builds the consolidated PM package workbook and flow doc; build_uk_caer_pm_master_control.mjs is the Node generator for the master-control dashboard with refresh triggers, update chain, and validation rows. Understanding these scripts is how an agent regenerates the artifacts after data changes.
tour.languageLesson: The package mixes Python builders (for openpyxl-style workbook generation and Markdown writing) with one Node .mjs builder for the master-control dashboard. The convention is one builder script per artifact, with helper functions for each tab/section and a main() entry that wires them together.

tour.title: Companion Project - Owen County Twin Shell
tour.description: The same workbench also seeds a second project, Owen County. Its Digital Twin Shell document establishes identity, twin boundary, authority stack, first twin records, seed risks, a floor maturity assessment, a starter set, and the first safe work plan. Reading this last shows how the doctrine from Step 2 instantiates into a new project from scratch.
